capabilities: Convert OPML outline files into Markdown notes split at a chosen level
Preview proposed file paths and inspect planned Markdown before writing
Resolve file name conflicts with numbered suffixes and skip existing destinations
Report parse errors, unsupported attributes, and parser limits
Save reusable import layouts and preview repeated imports with Pro
disambiguation: Not a feed-reader importer; it preserves outline text and URL attributes from the OPML file but does not download articles, subscribe to feeds, or import attachments.
extras: Freemium: saved layouts and repeat-import previews require a $5/month or $15 one-time GitHub Sponsors sponsorship, verified by device-flow sign-in; free core features work without any account. After updates it opens a What's new tab promoting other NoteMods plugins and Zovo Chat (dismissible). The README lists untested platforms and scenarios, and says files created before a storage error are not rolled back.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to convert OPML outline files into separate Markdown notes with preserved hierarchy.
summary: OPML importer that turns outline exports into ordered Markdown notes, creating one note per chosen outline level with child items as nested lists.
